digo_source: Pakia (2005) App. III, App. VI (+ Mgombato doka)
other_mijikenda: Duruma, Giriama: same name 'Mbugubugu' (Pakia App. VI)

teaser.en: A succulent vine whose fleshy stems snap at a touch, so the Digo call it 'breaking'.
teaser.sw: Mtambaa wenye mashina yenye maji mengi yanayokatika ukiyagusa tu, ndiyo maana Wadigo huuita 'kukatika'.

summary.en: Mdokadoka is a succulent climber of the grape family with thick, rounded leaves and brittle stems. Digo people share the name among three Cissus species and also call them mbugubugu, 'the climber'.
summary.sw: Mdokadoka ni mtambaa wenye maji mengi wa familia ya mizabibu, mwenye majani manene ya mviringo na mashina yanayovunjika kwa urahisi. Wadigo hulitumia jina hili kwa spishi tatu za *Cissus* na pia huziita *mbugubugu*, 'mtambaa'.

about.en: Mdokadoka is a succulent climber that scrambles over bushes with tendrils. Its stems are fleshy and somewhat angled, and they snap easily. The leaves are thick, almost round, waxy and bluish-green, with small teeth along the edge. Small greenish flowers in flat clusters are followed by round berries that ripen red. Pakia notes that *Cissus* species are among the few plants Digo people cannot tell apart by their leaves alone. They identify *mdokadoka* by its stem.
about.sw: Mdokadoka ni mtambaa wenye maji mengi unaotambaa juu ya vichaka kwa kutumia vikonyo. Mashina yake yana nyama na yana pembe kiasi, na hukatika kwa urahisi. Majani ni manene, karibu ya mviringo kamili, yenye nta na rangi ya kijani-samawati, yenye meno madogo pembeni. Maua madogo ya rangi ya kijani-kijani katika vishada bapa hufuatwa na matunda madogo ya mviringo yanayoiva yakawa mekundu. Pakia anabainisha kwamba spishi za *Cissus* ni miongoni mwa mimea michache ambayo Wadigo hawawezi kuitofautisha kwa majani peke yake. Huutambua *mdokadoka* kwa shina lake.

where.en: It grows in dry coastal bushland and thicket, often on coral rag or rocky ground, scrambling over shrubs.
where.sw: Hukua katika nyika kavu ya vichaka ya pwani na vichaka, mara nyingi kwenye ardhi ya matumbawe au yenye mawe, ukitambaa juu ya vichaka.

uses.en: Pakia records no use. In Arabia and the Horn of Africa the leaves of this species are cooked and eaten.
uses.sw: Pakia harekodi matumizi yoyote. Huko Uarabuni na Pembe ya Afrika majani ya spishi hii hupikwa na kuliwa.

culture.en: Pakia explains *mdokadoka* as 'breaking': the stem breaks (*doka*) easily. Mgombato glosses *doka* as 'to tear, to break off, to come apart'. The second name, *mbugubugu*, is the basic Digo word for a climber, built on the root *-bugu*. Doubling it stresses that the plant is the climber form.
culture.sw: Pakia anaeleza *mdokadoka* kuwa 'kukatika': shina hukatika (*doka*) kwa urahisi. Mgombato anaeleza *doka* kuwa 'kuchanika, kukatika, kutengana'. Jina la pili, *mbugubugu*, ni neno la msingi la Kidigo la mtambaa, lililojengwa juu ya mzizi *-bugu*. Kulirudia kunasisitiza kwamba mmea huu ni wa umbo la mtambaa.

names.en: Digo: *mdokadoka*, 'breaking', and *mbugubugu*, 'climber', shared with Duruma and Giriama. Pakia gives both names to three species: *Cissus rotundifolia*, *C. sylvicola* and *C. quinquangularis*. The name *dokadoka*, without the *m-*, belongs to a *Tylophora* climber. No English or Swahili name is recorded by Pakia.
names.sw: Kidigo: *mdokadoka*, 'kukatika', na *mbugubugu*, 'mtambaa', linaloshirikiwa na Kiduruma na Kigiriama. Pakia anatoa majina yote mawili kwa spishi tatu: *Cissus rotundifolia*, *C. sylvicola* na *C. quinquangularis*. Jina *dokadoka*, bila *m-*, ni la mtambaa wa *Tylophora*. Pakia harekodi jina la Kiingereza wala la Kiswahili.

reason.en: Dokadoka, the same 'breaking' name for a Tylophora
reason.sw: Dokadoka, jina lile lile la 'kukatika' kwa Tylophora

reason.en: Wild grape, in the same family
reason.sw: Mzabibu mwitu (wild grape), wa familia hiyo hiyo

mgombato: doka to tear, to break off, to come apart (e.g. a piece of rope); kukatika.
